chapter: Learning, lawn parties and band rivalries
title: Pelican band on the road; Robichaux's country band
summary: Dawson says he played mostly with Dusen and Clem's Pelican band, on the road all week, and that Robichaux's reading band also toured the country.

story.theme_name: Life on the road: touring bands, buses and one-nighters
story.community_name: Life on the road: buses, trains and one-nighters

blocks.x: Did you play very often with Buddy Bowling?

No. He had his own line up. I never, I never played with him. I played more with Frankie Deucing, with, uh, Edward Clemmen, them, with that Pelican band. I played a long time with them. They kept, they, uh, they played, they used to go up in the country.
They kept that ice seat. They was, they, they was on that road every, every day, every night. The whole week they'd be gone on that road. From one place to the other.
Weren't you saying that Robichaux went on the road?

Robichaux had a country band too. He all around, uh, up, up around Byler's Push, you know. And, uh, up around La Coman, uh, Byler's Coman, uh, and then people up there was crazy about old John Robichaux's band. He's a left hand violin player, you know.
